title: What training do assisted living (RCFE) staff need in California?
description: California RCFE staff training under H&S Code 1569.625: 40 hours initial, 20 hours a year, 12 dementia hours, medication training and Title 22 records.
shortAnswer: In California, staff of a residential care facility for the elderly (RCFE) who help residents with personal activities of daily living need 40 hours of training: 20 hours, including 6 hours of dementia care, before working independently and 20 more within the first four weeks. After that they need 20 hours every year, including 8 hours of dementia care. Health and Safety Code 1569.625 and 1569.626 set these figures, and CDSS Title 22 regulations set content and records.
keyTakeaways: Health and Safety Code 1569.625(b) requires 40 hours of initial training for direct care staff, 20 before working independently and 20 within four weeks, with 16 hours specified as hands-on training.
Annual training is 20 hours, of which 8 hours must be dementia care and 4 hours postural supports, restricted health conditions and hospice care.

Staff who assist with self-administration of medications need separate training under 1569.69: 24 hours in facilities licensed for 16 or more, 10 hours in facilities for 15 or fewer, an examination, then 8 hours each year.

Certified nurse assistants, licensed vocational nurses and registered nurses are largely exempt from 1569.625 but still need 8 hours of facility orientation; nurse assistants also need the dementia hours and annual training.
As at November 2026, CDSS dementia care regulations in effect since January 1, 2025 require each facility's plan of operation to include a staff training plan meeting these statutes.
regulator: California Department of Social Services (CDSS), Community Care Licensing Division
appliesTo: Licensed residential care facilities for the elderly (RCFEs), commonly called assisted living or board and care
RCFE staff who assist residents with personal activities of daily living (direct care staff)
Staff who assist residents with the self-administration of medications
RCFE administrators holding or seeking a CDSS administrator certificate

sections.heading: Where do California's RCFE training rules come from?

blocks.text: From two layers. The California Residential Care Facilities for the Elderly Act in the Health and Safety Code sets the hours: [section 1569.625](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=1569.625) for general direct care training, [section 1569.626](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=1569.626) for dementia care training, and [section 1569.69](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=1569.69) for medication assistance training. The California Department of Social Services (CDSS) implements them through California Code of Regulations, Title 22, Division 6, Chapter 8, which CDSS publishes on its [regulations page](https://www.cdss.ca.gov/inforesources/Rules-Regulations/Legislation-and-Regulations/Community-Care-Licensing-Regulations/Residential).

Section 87411(c) of Title 22 requires all RCFE staff who assist residents with personal activities of daily living to receive initial and annual training "as specified in Health and Safety Code sections 1569.625 and 1569.69." One detail matters for audits: the records regulation, 87412(c)(1)(A), still describes documentation of at least ten hours of initial training within four weeks and four hours annually. That wording predates the current statutory hours, so facilities should plan to the statute and document against it. This page reflects the law as at November 2026.

sections.heading: How many hours of initial training do RCFE direct care staff need?

blocks.text: Forty hours, split across two deadlines. Under 1569.625(b)(1), a staff member must complete 20 hours before working independently with residents, including 6 hours specific to dementia care under 1569.626(a) and 4 hours specific to postural supports, restricted health conditions and hospice care under 1569.696(a). The remaining 20 hours, including 6 more hours of dementia care, must be completed within the first four weeks of employment.

The statute allows coursework through lectures, instructional videos and interactive online courses, and specifies that 16 hours shall be hands-on training. The section has been operative since January 1, 2016.

blocks.title: Health and Safety Code 1569.625(c): required content
blocks.text: The training shall include, but not be limited to: physical limitations and needs of the elderly; importance and techniques for personal care services; residents' rights; policies and procedures regarding medications; psychosocial needs of the elderly; building and fire safety and the appropriate response to emergencies; dementia care, including the use and misuse of antipsychotics and the adverse effects of psychotropic drugs; the special needs of persons with Alzheimer's disease and dementia, including nonpharmacologic, person-centered approaches; and cultural competency and sensitivity in issues relating to the underserved, aging, lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transgender community.

Title 22 section 87411(c) adds that staff providing care must receive appropriate first aid training from persons qualified by agencies such as the American Red Cross, and that training must include recognizing signs and symptoms of dementia.

Twenty hours every year. Under 1569.625(b)(2), direct care staff need an additional 20 hours annually, of which 8 hours must be dementia care training under 1569.626 and 4 hours must cover postural supports, restricted health conditions and hospice care under 1569.696. Annual training may be on the job, in a classroom or both, and may include online training.

Section 1569.626(a)(2) says the 8 annual dementia hours must be developed in consultation with individuals or organizations with specific expertise in dementia care, or by an outside source with that expertise. The training may be completed in one day or over time, at the facility or offsite, and may combine observation and practical application. For choosing refresh intervals across a whole catalog, see [how to set mandatory training refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles).

sections.heading: Do certified nurse assistants and nurses need the 40 hours?

blocks.text: Mostly not, but they are not fully exempt. Section 1569.625(d) excludes certified nurse assistants, licensed vocational nurses and registered nurses from the section, with two exceptions.

items: Any licensed or certified health professional must receive 8 hours of training on resident characteristics, resident records and facility practices and procedures before providing direct care to residents.
A certified nurse assistant must also receive the 12 hours of dementia care training in 1569.626 and the 20 hours of annual training in 1569.625(b)(2).

blocks.text: Facilities that hire nurse assistants trained under federal nursing home rules should not assume that training transfers. The federal program is described on the [nurse aide training and competency evaluation page](/regulations/nurse-aide-training-and-competency-evaluation).

sections.heading: What extra training do staff who assist with medications need?

blocks.text: A separate program under [Health and Safety Code 1569.69](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=1569.69), on top of the direct care hours. The initial training depends on facility size:

items: Facilities licensed for 16 or more: 24 hours, consisting of 16 hours of hands-on shadowing training completed before assisting with self-administration of medications, and 8 hours of other training completed within the first four weeks.
Facilities licensed for 15 or fewer: 10 hours, consisting of 6 hours of hands-on shadowing training before assisting, and 4 hours of other training within the first two weeks.

Each employee must pass an examination testing comprehension of and competency in the listed subjects, which include medication orders, storage, side effects, and the increased risk of death when elderly residents with dementia are given antipsychotic medications.
After passing, employees who continue to assist with medications need 8 hours of in-service training on medication-related issues in each succeeding 12-month period.
The initial training must be repeated after a break in service of more than 180 consecutive calendar days with the same licensee, or on moving to another licensee.

blocks.text: Trainers must meet education and experience criteria in 1569.69(e), and training materials and the examination must be developed by, or in consultation with, a licensed nurse, pharmacist or physician.

sections.heading: What changed in the 2025 dementia care regulations?

blocks.text: CDSS updated its RCFE dementia care regulations effective January 1, 2025, announced in [PIN 24-09-ASC](https://www.cdss.ca.gov/Portals/9/CCLD/Dementia%20Care%20Information%20Webpage/241216%20PIN%2024-09-ASC%20UPDATED%20DEMENTIA%20CARE%20AND%20MISC%20REGULATIONS%20FOR%20RCFES%20(For%20Release-A).pdf). Section 87705(b)(1) now requires licensees to ensure staff receive training, as part of the plan of operation's training requirements, in dementia care (hydration, nutrition, skin care, communication, therapeutic activities, behavioral challenges, the environment and activities of daily living), recognizing symptoms that may create or aggravate behavioral expression such as dehydration, urinary tract infections and swallowing problems, and recognizing the effects of medications commonly used to reduce behavioral expression.

Former section 87707, which set separate training for facilities advertising dementia special care, was repealed because it contained outdated training requirements. Under section 87208(a)(6), every facility's plan of operation must include a plan for training staff as required by Health and Safety Code 1569.625, 1569.626 and 1569.69 and Title 22 sections 87411 and 87705. CDSS maintains guidance on its [dementia care information page](https://www.cdss.ca.gov/inforesources/dementia-care-information-and-resources).

sections.heading: What should an RCFE's training records show?

blocks.text: A licensing analyst can compare hire dates, first independent shifts and training dates, so the file must make each deadline visible. Section 87412(c)(2) requires documentation of the trainer's full name, subjects covered, dates of attendance and hours per subject, and 87411(c)(6) requires a note of which trainer qualification criterion was met. sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry maps each 1569.625(c) topic and each 87705 dementia topic to learning outcomes and to the hour buckets they count toward, so a facility can see whether a new hire's first 20 hours actually include the dementia and postural support content the statute requires before independent work. See [healthcare and life sciences](/industries/healthcare-life-sciences).

faqs.q: Can RCFE staff training be completed online in California?
faqs.a: Partly. 1569.625(b)(1) allows lectures, instructional videos and interactive online courses for coursework, but specifies 16 hours as hands-on training. Annual training under (b)(2) may include online training. Medication assistance training requires hands-on shadowing before an employee assists with medications.

faqs.q: Does dementia training count toward the 40 hours or come on top?
faqs.a: It counts toward them. The 12 dementia hours in 1569.626 are built into the 40-hour structure in 1569.625(b)(1): 6 within the first 20 hours before independent work and 6 within the remaining 20 hours. The 8 annual dementia hours likewise sit within the 20 annual hours.

faqs.q: Do medication assistance hours count toward the 40 hours?
faqs.a: 1569.69(a)(7) states that its training requirements are not intended to replace or supplant the training required of staff who assist with personal activities of daily living under 1569.625 and 1569.696. Facilities should treat medication training as a separate requirement with its own records.

faqs.q: How much continuing education does an RCFE administrator need?
faqs.a: Under 1569.616(f), an administrator certificate is renewed every two years on completion of 40 hours of continuing education related to the uniform core of knowledge, with no more than half through self-paced courses. Initial certification requires an 80-hour program with at least 60 hours of interactive instruction.

HSC 1569.69: 24 hours (16 shadowing + 8) for facilities of 16 or more; 10 hours (6 + 4) for 15 or fewer; examination; 8 hours annual in-service; repeat after break over 180 days or new licensee; (a)(7) does not replace 1569.625 training.
